title: Vyshka state snapshot envelope bodies
description: Machine-readable companion to spec/protocol.md section 8.3. The prose document is normative: where the two disagree, the prose wins. Like the other schema documents this is a library of definitions with no root constraint: reference `#/$defs/statePlayers`, `#/$defs/stateVehicles`, `#/$defs/stateEntities`, and `#/$defs/stateWorld` for the plugin -> hub bodies and `#/$defs/stateReject` for the hub -> plugin refusal.

playerRef.title: Platform-qualified player identity
playerRef.description: The player reference shape of section 8.2, shared by every protocol payload that names a player.

position.description: Two or three finite numbers in the game's own map frame. Advisory, for display; the hub never interprets it.

playerEntry.title: One player in a state.players snapshot

name.description: Display name at capture time. Advisory: identity lives in `player`.

data.description: Game- or mod-specific extras. Absent and null both read as an empty object.

objectEntry.title: One vehicle or entity in a snapshot

id.description: Stable for the lifetime of the thing it names, so consecutive snapshots can be correlated.

data.description: Game- or mod-specific extras. Absent and null both read as an empty object.

capturedAt.description: When the game sampled this state. Optional: absent, unparseable, or implausibly far ahead of the hub's clock, the envelope's ts stands in, with the section 4 receipt-time substitution behind that.

statePlayers.title: state.players body
statePlayers.description: Plugin -> hub. The full current player list; it replaces its predecessor entirely, and an empty array is a meaningful snapshot (nobody online). Applied or rejected whole; caps: 262144 bytes, 5000 entries.

stateVehicles.title: state.vehicles body
stateVehicles.description: Plugin -> hub. The full current vehicle list, same replacement and whole-application rules as state.players.

stateEntities.title: state.entities body
stateEntities.description: Plugin -> hub. The full current list of everything else worth mapping, same replacement and whole-application rules as state.players.

worldState.title: The world in a state.world snapshot
worldState.description: One object, not a list: a server has one world. A member absent from it is not reported, never zero or false; an empty object is a snapshot that reports nothing.

time.description: The game's own clock, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with no offset, naming a valid calendar date and time of day. The game's calendar, not a moment on any real clock: the hub checks the form and never compares it with its own clock or with capturedAt.

data.description: Game- or mod-specific extras (the weather, how fast the clock runs, a season). Absent and null both read as an empty object.

stateWorld.title: state.world body
stateWorld.description: Plugin -> hub. The world as it stands; it replaces its predecessor entirely. Applied or rejected whole; cap: 262144 bytes.

stateReject.title: state.reject body
stateReject.description: Hub -> plugin, queued when a snapshot was refused. Envelope-level success like the rejections of sections 6.4 and 8.1: the refused envelope is still acked, the stored state did not change, and the plugin must not treat this as a transport error.

envelopeId.description: The id of the state.* envelope this rejection answers.

path.description: A path into the rejected body, such as players[3].player. Empty when the fault is the body as a whole.

errors.description: Bounded by the hub (reference cap 20 entries).
